subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` adopt a hard 1 MiB public input limit that rejects previously accepted larger regular files?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes a public CLI contract rather than mechanically fixing an established limit, and repository policy treats CLI setup and externally copied command flows as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Preserve existing input compatibility
options.body: Do not merge the 1 MiB rejection; pursue a bounded implementation only if it retains the established accepted-file behavior.

options.title: Approve a documented 1 MiB limit
options.body: Accept the new failure mode as a deliberate CLI contract and require user-facing documentation plus upgrade and real-behavior evidence before merge.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing input compatibility
recommendation.body: Do not merge the 1 MiB rejection; pursue a bounded implementation only if it retains the established accepted-file behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline indicates direct involvement, and this is an API/product compatibility decision rather than a test-only repair.
